newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl urges reasonable Krupp, Thyssen solution.
newsitem.headline: Kohl urges reasonable Krupp, Thyssen solution.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl urged steel makers Krupp and Thyssen, facing a choice between cooperation or a hostile takeover, to find a reasonable solution, the Bild newspaper reported on Wednesday.

In an advance excerpt from its Thursday edition, Bild quoted Kohl as saying, "In the interest of those employed by both companies and in the interest of the economic climate in our country, the issue is to find a reasonable solution."
Kohl urged both parties "to live up to their total responsibilities".

Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp and Thyssen said earlier they would hold eight days of talks aimed at founding a joint steel company, but that if the talks failed they would return to their original standoff.

On Tuesday, Thyssen vowed to defend itself against a rare 13.6 billion mark ($8.1 billion) hostile takeover bid by its smaller rival Krupp. Thyssen said tens of thousands of steel jobs hang in the balance.
-- Terence Gallagher, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-2609750 ($ = 1.674 German Marks)
